key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and physical consistency constraints are more effective during fine-tuning than during early or full-training use.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable inter-patient prediction of aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD solutions on SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Evaluate active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints to improve data efficiency and physical consistency.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic field evaluations show fine-tuning gains from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric coverage as the main limitation.
watch_item: Generalization remains limited by the geometric support of the anatomy parametrization; the abstract provides no quantitative error or speedup metrics.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
